nodes.question: How do we turn a functional idea into reliable working digital hardware, from HDL to physical integrated circuits?
nodes.why: The same behavior must satisfy logic, state, timing, electrical, toolchain, fabrication and verification constraints.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Use function, state, timing, interfaces and physical implementation as composable—not interchangeable—contracts.
unresolved_questions: The linked chapter is a retrieval lead; substantive validation or implementation is not yet documented.

nodes.question: What is the actual path from HDL and simulation to a physical FPGA?
nodes.why: Code describes behavior; the FPGA configuration depends on synthesis, technology mapping, placement, routing, timing and board constraints.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The 2008 text shows HDL → synthesis/implementation → device programming on Spartan-3/ISE. Contemporary systems keep the conceptual pipeline but require a platform-specific implementation and bitstream flow.

technical_distinctions.mechanism: An RTL simulation models specified behavior while the implemented circuit occupies particular cells and wires with delays.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Does a representative design pass both a behavioral run and board-level I/O/timing?

nodes.minimum_reconstruction_probe: Implement one clocked counter on an available board, inspect actual mapped resources and the timing report, and verify pin behavior.
unresolved_questions: Which target family, toolchain, and concrete constraints make this explanation insufficient for a present-day device?

nodes.question: Why can a Verilog combinational block accidentally remember something?
nodes.why: Incomplete assignments can synthesize an unexpected latch; text shape and intended truth table can diverge.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu's RT-level combinational discussion explicitly identifies incomplete branch/output assignment as a way an internal state element or feedback is inferred. Conditional control logic maps to mux/priority structures; a source-level if is not necessarily an instruction executed by a CPU.

source_sections.section: Ch. 3, incomplete branch/output assignment and combinational always blocks

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A combinational output is fully determined by present inputs; a latch retains earlier information when enable conditions hold.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Enumerate input combinations, inspect whether every output gets a value, and compare synthesized storage elements.

nodes.minimum_reconstruction_probe: Synthesize two otherwise similar blocks with and without a missing assignment and inspect the inferred components.
unresolved_questions: Which target family, toolchain, and concrete constraints make this explanation insufficient for a present-day device?

nodes.question: How can logic remember history and respond to events?
nodes.why: Registers and finite-state machines express different reusable patterns for state evolution.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Counters and shift registers have regular next-state operations; finite-state machines encode irregular control transitions. Correctness requires explicit reset behavior and observation of state transitions in the intended clock domain.

source_sections.section: Ch. 4, flip-flop/register, counter, FIFO and timing

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A behavioral control state can be encoded differently in flip-flops without changing its visible transition contract.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Can a trace of inputs, clocks, current state and outputs reconstruct every transition?

nodes.minimum_reconstruction_probe: Implement a debounce-and-edge detector and distinguish contact chatter from unintended repeated state changes.
unresolved_questions: Which target family, toolchain, and concrete constraints make this explanation insufficient for a present-day device?

nodes.question: When should I separate a controller from a datapath?
nodes.why: An FSMD combines conditional state sequencing with register-transfer operations; a chip datapath and controller can be designed as separate contracts.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu's preface and Ch. 6 outline register-transfer FSMD organization; Mead–Conway Chs. 3, 5 and 6 show how data paths, state and controller choices shape integrated computer structures.

nodes.question: Why can a circuit work in simulation but fail at speed?
nodes.why: Flip-flops require setup/hold; a combinational path and clock distribution bound safe sampling.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu's synchronous circuit discussion separates clock-to-Q, propagation and setup/hold timing. Implementable clock rate depends on the particular mapped path, not the developer's intended nominal frequency.

nodes.question: How can a receiver reconstruct bits when the wire carries no clock?
nodes.why: UART receiver estimates bit centers from start-edge timing, baud-rate agreement and oversampling.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu's UART section uses 16x baud oversampling to estimate serial bit centers; its baud generator produces one-clock enables rather than a second physical clock domain. Incorrect tick rates or framing can corrupt serial interpretation.

nodes.question: How do on-chip FPGA memories and an external RAM change the design?
nodes.why: An RTL memory can map to registers, block RAM or external SRAM, each with distinct port and timing contracts.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The source's Chs. 11–12 distinguish external asynchronous SRAM-controller access timing from Spartan-3 specific internal memory usage. Neither inference nor pin-level memory behavior is guaranteed by a plain array declaration.

nodes.question: How can external electrical events become reliable device interfaces?
nodes.why: Physical signaling, protocol state and host/device role are distinct contracts.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu Chs. 9–10 implement PS/2 keyboard and mouse protocols with scan-code interpretation and bidirectional roles. Examples are valuable protocol state machines but the particular physical ports may be absent on newer boards.

nodes.question: How can logic draw pictures or text on a display?
nodes.why: Pixels require coordinated spatial addressing, scan timing and data bandwidth, not simply writing a 2D array.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu's Chs. 13–14 build VGA graphics synchronization and text/tile addressing. Their legacy VGA electrical and timing interface illustrates constraints that HDMI, DisplayPort and modern display pipelines implement differently.

source_sections.section: Ch. 14, VGA text and tile-mapped graphics

technical_distinctions.mechanism: A framebuffer/tilemap specifies pixels; a video interface specifies when and how those pixels are transmitted.
technical_distinctions.discriminating_observation: Can the implementation meet pixel timing while concurrent logic updates display data?

nodes.minimum_reconstruction_probe: Render a moving tile on a real display, observe blanking and verify that buffer reads meet pixel-rate timing.
unresolved_questions: The linked chapter is a retrieval lead; substantive validation or implementation is not yet documented.

nodes.question: When should the hardware contain a programmable CPU instead of hardwired control?
nodes.why: A soft-core executes stored instructions; an FSM or dedicated datapath implements a narrower workload directly.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Chu Chs. 15–18 introduce PicoBlaze, assembly, I/O and interrupts; Mead–Conway Chs. 5–6 illustrate a datapath/controller composition. A processor trades instruction overhead and state for programmability, not automatic improvement.

nodes.question: How do a handful of transistors become gates with real delays?
nodes.why: MOS gate voltage controls conduction; capacitance and transistor/current limits shape digital switching.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Mead–Conway Ch. 1 explains MOS switching, inverter operation, loading and delay. A Boolean '1' abstracts away analog transfer curves, transition times, power and noise margins.

nodes.question: Why can two electrically equivalent gate networks have very different physical quality?
nodes.why: Transistor geometry, wire lengths, contacts, signal loading and design rules shape speed/area/yield.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: The VLSI text spans symbolic layout and design-rule layers rather than treating gates as zero-area symbols; the same netlist can be physically arranged with different parasitic load and routing costs.

nodes.question: Why can a circuit design be correct but fail to become a reliable chip?
nodes.why: Wafer-patterning steps, layer alignment and random defects constrain whether designed circuit patterns become functional devices.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Mead–Conway Ch. 2 covers nMOS process and yield statistics, and Ch. 4 layout-to-fabrication. Historical process rules are illustrative: a modern fabrication requires the actual target foundry PDK, DRC and signoff flow.

nodes.question: What can a clock coordinate, and what happens when timing assumptions fail?
nodes.why: Distributed clocks skew; asynchronous events can violate sampling assumptions; handshake/self-timed approaches exchange global clock assumptions for protocol constraints.
nodes.mechanism_explanation: Mead–Conway Ch. 7 discusses clock distribution, synchronization failure and self-timed signaling. A synchronizer may lower failure probability, but cannot remove metastability from physics.

relations.why: State is the new mechanism beyond a total combinational input-output mapping
Control state determines register-transfer steps and datapath operations
Technology-mapped logic has physically measurable paths and timing requirements
Bit-center sampling and baud-rate ticks depend on a clocking contract
Serial framing is one example of protocol state and physical transport
Pixel generation must satisfy access patterns and scanout bandwidth
A stored-program controller and dedicated datapath can realize related behavior under different cost conditions
Analog switching and load effects depend on physical connectivity and geometry
Physical layout must satisfy a real fabrication process and its design rules
Clock skew, metastability and handshake behavior change timing guarantees
Configuring premanufactured LUT fabric is different from manufacturing a custom transistor pattern
